scope: OLP-0606 proof inference patterns from definitions through existential claims; state-only draft

additional_semantic_checks: The opening separates already available assumptions or derived facts from the new inference and its justification; induction is only deferred to a later discussion.
Applying equality definition to established D=E and using it as a proof goal are distinct directions. The (a)/(b) template and quoted proof preserve both containment directions.
Conjunction elimination and conjunction introduction are separate patterns. Disjunction introduction needs one disjunct, while the source notes cases are often useful for mixed cases.
All formulations p only if q, q if p, and q provided p have the p→q direction; iff needs both directions or a genuine biconditional chain.
The universal proof fixes arbitrary x and does not choose a special witness; the example establishes A subseteq A union B.
Case analysis uses p or q as a premise and proves r from each. The B/C-to-D/E example keeps (a)-(d), two cases, and the editorial footnote outside the proof logic.
The singleton witness A={x} proof separately establishes A nonempty and A subseteq B; no assumption of these properties is smuggled in.

An existential witness name must be fresh and absent from the discharged conclusion. The corrected prose distinguishes independence of the arbitrary witness from dependence on the existential premise.
The final quoted proof is intentionally invalid because two existential claims can have different witnesses; no repair to its reasoning is inserted.
Three visible corrections address the omitted x in two membership expressions, witness-scope overstatement, and wrong x/A variable in the nonempty-set equivalence.

intentional_foreign_literals.reason: The source explicitly teaches this English abbreviation for the biconditional and the Gujarati text explains it.
